messages.subject: Extended, multi-application session support?
parts:
Greetings!

I have a cmd-line driven exploratory environment, in the same vein as GUI-based RCommander, within which the user will be running any number of connected application executions utilizing the results from previous executions.  Is Shiny suitable for this kind of environment?

Thanks,
Doug

parts: OK. Well, do take a look at the Radyant stuff, and I'm sure we will have more interface-heavy examples of Shiny apps in the future. Good luck!

On Tue, May 7, 2013 at 12:14 PM, Doug Elias <del...@ithaca.edu> wrote:
I don't know anything about Deducer ... Rcommander and ... now I'm blanking on it, but there's another R-environment that I looked at, and they both have a rather steep 'inclusion' curve, the kinds of things I'd have to go back and re-do in order to play nicely in those sandboxes.  And they're designed around 'knowledge level' assumptions that would be a ... contorted fit to my stuff.  I'll have to design an interface to them in order to be able to work with their data and apps and results, but, again, that's farther down the development path.

ANYway ... you've given me some more stuff to work on and investigate, and I'm re-opening the tcl/tk approach and may simply bite-the-bullet and complete that for this version, then re-think things. 

Just have to do SOMEthing, get off my ass and get moving ...

Thanks again,
Doug


On Tue, May 7, 2013 at 2:57 PM, Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
I don't think reinstalling RStudio will help. What version of R do you have installed on Ubuntu?

I can't say that something as complicated as Rcommander is in the "sweet spot" of what we're trying to accomplish with Shiny. However, I don't know of any limitations in Shiny that would prevent you from doing so. Vincent Nijs has built probably the most complicated Shiny app so far, you can see it here.

That being said, tcl/tk or even conventional web development techniques plus something like OpenCPU, are probably going to be less risky, though probably more work and more difficult to manage complexity-wise. In other words, I believe Shiny might be easier and more robust until you hit its limitations, which we don't really know yet what they are.

Sorry not to have a more definitive answer for you. Would it be possible to just use Rcommander or Deducer as they exist today, and write a plugin that works with one of them?


On Tue, May 7, 2013 at 6:05 AM, Doug Elias <del...@ithaca.edu> wrote:
I've got some kind of cruft in my Ubuntu environment, because I tried exactly the same thing on my Win7 system right 'next-door' and running the install packages command from the tools drop-down to grab 'shiny' worked just fine, found and d/l'd httpuv no problem.  So it's something in particular to junk screwing up the works in that system, and I'm trying to find a way to clear things out without having to completely re-install RStudio ... which I'll do, if I have to, just using this as a 'learning experience' about the environment.  Any insights would be appreciated.

So ... you're probably familiar with Rcommander; would 'shiny' be an appropriate platform for an environment like that?  My project is very analogous, and all I'm basically looking for is a way to simplify the graphics-interface level programming I'm having to get involved in, moving from pure cmd-line to a GUI.  I'm already a fair distance along a tcl/tk path, having mapped out an input/processing/output separation strategy for the modules and building some test modules to see how things actually work, but it'll be a not-inconsiderable effort to make the necessary mods.  'Shiny' might be able to save me some work, plus it adds the web aspect which I'd put farther down the development path.  Anyway, again: any insights would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks for your comments,
Doug
